page.overview:
Who is Jo Gartner?

Josef Gartner (born 24 January 1954 and died 1 June 1986) was an Austrian Formula One driver who raced part-time in . He finished in the top five at the 1984 Italian Grand Prix, but was not eligible to score points since Osella had only entered one car to the championship.

He was killed while racing in the 1986 24 Hours of Le Mans after his car suffered an unknown mechanical failure.

In 1972, Gartner began working in motorsport with the Kaimann Formula Super Vee team in a technical role. He began participating racing in hillclimb events in 1976 before entering the 1977 European Formula Super Vee championship where he finished third in the championship.

Two years later, he advanced to the European Formula Three Championship before driving a two-year-old in Formula Two. He was invited to the BMW M1 Procar Championship replacing Markus Höttinger, who was killed by a detached wheel from Derek Warwick's crashed car. Gartner had made his debut in that race, along damaging his car on debris from the incident.
